At the moment of import, importers shall provide verifiable appropriate evidence, to prove the country in which raw steel or iron was initially produced in liquid form within a steel- or iron-making furnace and subsequently cast into its first solid state (‘country of ‘melt and pour’).
The country of ‘melt and pour’ shall be declared by means of one of the TARIC document codes Y376 to Y388.
The appropriate evidence, to prove the country of melt and pour shall be declared by means of one of the TARIC document codes C131 to C139.
Failure to declare the country of ‘melt and pour’ and the related evidence shall lead to a rejection of the import.

From 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028, a customs duty of EUR 3 per item in a consignment the intrinsic value of which does not exceed a total of EUR 150 shall apply instead of the relief eliminated pursuant to Article 1 of this Regulation, where:
(a) the importation of the goods is exempt from VAT in accordance with Article 143(1), point (ca), of Directive 2006/112/EC; or
(b) the goods are in a postal consignment as defined in Article 1, point (24), of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/2446.

footnotes.text:
Article 2a of Regulation 2023/956:
An importer, including any importer with the status of an authorised CBAM declarant, shall be exempted from
the obligations under this Regulation, where the net mass of the imported goods in a given calendar year does not
cumulatively exceed the single mass-based threshold laid down in point 1 of Annex VII (the “single mass-based
threshold”). That threshold shall apply to the total net mass of goods under all CN codes aggregated per importer and
per calendar year. In such a case, the importer, including an importer with the status of an authorised CBAM declarant,
shall declare that exemption in the relevant customs declaration.

CBAM obligations do not apply to goods of EU origin, and in cases where non-CBAM goods of non-EU origin are processed together with EU-origin goods under the inward processing procedure, the resulting processed CBAM goods released for free circulation shall be excluded from CBAM obligations.

Article 17.7a. of Regulation 2023/956: By way of derogation from Article 4, where an importer or an indirect customs representative has submitted an application in accordance with Article 5 by 31 March 2026, such an importer or indirect customs representative may provisionally continue to import goods until the competent authority takes a decision under this Article.

International organisations may benefit from exemptions from customs duties and taxes, as well as from applicable prohibitions and restrictions on imports, where provided for by the relevant international or headquarters agreement. Such exemptions are, inter alia, provided for in respect of ITER under Article 6 of the Agreement on the Privileges and Immunities of the ITER International Fusion Energy Organization for the Joint Implementation of the ITER Project (OJ L 358, 16.12.2006).
Legal base: https://www.iter.org/sites/default/files/ITER%20Agreement%20PI%20EN.pdf

Regulation (EU) 2023/956 - Article 25: Without prejudice to Article 2a, the customs authorities shall not allow the importation of goods by any person other than an authorised CBAM declarant.
This Regulation shall not apply to:
- goods to be moved or used in the context of military activities pursuant to Article 1, point (49), of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/2446,
- electricity generated on the continental shelf or in the exclusive economic zone of a Member State or of a country or territory listed in points 1 and 2 of Annex III;
- hydrogen originating on the continental shelf or in the exclusive economic zone of a Member State or of a country or territory listed in point 1 of Annex III.’;
- an importer, where the net mass of the imported goods in a given calendar year does not cumulatively exceed the single mass-based threshold laid down in point 1 of Annex VII (the “single mass-based threshold”).
Regulation (EU) 2023/956 - Article 2.4 – Scope:
Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall not apply to goods originating in the third countries and territories listed in point 1 of Annex III.

the obligations under this Regulation, where the net mass of the imported goods in a given calendar year does not
cumulatively exceed the single mass-based threshold laid down in point 1 of Annex VII (the “single mass-based
threshold”). That threshold shall apply to the total net mass of goods under all CN codes aggregated per importer and
per calendar year. In such a case, the importer, including an importer with the status of an authorised CBAM declarant,
shall declare that exemption in the relevant customs declaration.

CBAM obligations do not apply to goods of EU origin, and in cases where non-CBAM goods of non-EU origin are processed together with EU-origin goods under the inward processing procedure, the resulting processed CBAM goods released for free circulation shall be excluded from CBAM obligations.

Article 17.7a. of Regulation 2023/956: By way of derogation from Article 4, where an importer or an indirect customs representative has submitted an application in accordance with Article 5 by 31 March 2026, such an importer or indirect customs representative may provisionally continue to import goods until the competent authority takes a decision under this Article.

International organisations may benefit from exemptions from customs duties and taxes, as well as from applicable prohibitions and restrictions on imports, where provided for by the relevant international or headquarters agreement. Such exemptions are, inter alia, provided for in respect of ITER under Article 6 of the Agreement on the Privileges and Immunities of the ITER International Fusion Energy Organization for the Joint Implementation of the ITER Project (OJ L 358, 16.12.2006).
Legal base: https://www.iter.org/sites/default/files/ITER%20Agreement%20PI%20EN.pdf

Regulation (EU) 2023/956 - Article 25: Without prejudice to Article 2a, the customs authorities shall not allow the importation of goods by any person other than an authorised CBAM declarant.
This Regulation shall not apply to:
- goods to be moved or used in the context of military activities pursuant to Article 1, point (49), of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/2446,
- electricity generated on the continental shelf or in the exclusive economic zone of a Member State or of a country or territory listed in points 1 and 2 of Annex III;
- hydrogen originating on the continental shelf or in the exclusive economic zone of a Member State or of a country or territory listed in point 1 of Annex III.’;
- an importer, where the net mass of the imported goods in a given calendar year does not cumulatively exceed the single mass-based threshold laid down in point 1 of Annex VII (the “single mass-based threshold”).
Regulation (EU) 2023/956 - Article 2.4 – Scope:
Regulation (EU) 2023/956 shall not apply to goods originating in the third countries and territories listed in point 1 of Annex III.
